name: Brazil beyond Rio: Salvador, the Bahian coast, Lencois Maran

destination.name: Brazil beyond Rio: Salvador, the Bahian coast, Lencois Maran
destination.pitch: Three different countries stitched by long domestic flights: pick Salvador plus one of the other two unless you have a full twelve nights on the ground and go between May and September when the Lencois lagoons are actually full.

because.nature: The Lencois dune field with rain-fed lagoons between May and September, and the Rio Negro flooded forest, are two of the strangest landscapes in South America.
because.exploration: Every leg needs a 4x4, a voadeira speedboat, a catamaran or a lodge canoe, and the places worth going have no road.
because.food: Acaraje from a baiana's pan in Rio Vermelho, moqueca cooked in dende, and in Manaus tambaqui ribs, tucuma and tacaca at dusk on the Largo.
because.relaxation: Morro de Sao Paulo has no cars and Quarta Praia is a long empty walk at low tide.
because.culture: Salvador is the centre of Afro-Brazilian Brazil: candomble, capoeira, Olodum drums every Tuesday in Pelourinho.
because.adventure: The Lencois crossing to Queimada dos Britos on foot, night caiman spotting by canoe, and piranha fishing in the igapo are real, not staged.
because.city: Salvador has the churches and the music but the city is spread out, hot, and needs taxis; Manaus is a working port, not a destination.

destination.caveat: The three regions do not chain cheaply: Salvador to Sao Luis is a two-hour nonstop but Sao Luis to Manaus needs a connection through Belem or Brasilia, the Lencois lagoons are dry from roughly November to April, a jungle lodge costs more per night than everything else combined, and Pelourinho after  Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

cities.name: Salvador
cities.base: Rio Vermelho: the acaraje square, the restaurants and bars locals actually use, and a 15-minute ride to Pelourinho, which is worth visiting by day and on Tuesday night but is not where you want to wal

cities.name: Morro de Sao Paulo
cities.base: Terceira Praia: quiet at night, sand path to the Segunda Praia bars, and the boats for Garapua and Boipeba leave from the beach in front. The island has no cars and the TUPA entry tax is R$90 per pers

cities.name: Barreirinhas
cities.base: Avenida Beira Rio in Barreirinhas for tour logistics and a 30-minute 4x4 to the Lagoa Azul gate; Atins (a 90-minute speedboat downriver, sand streets, no bank) if you want to wake up next to the dunes

cities.name: Lencois Maranhenses National Park
cities.base: No beds inside the park except hammocks in the oasis settlements on the guided crossing. Everything is a 4x4 or boat day from Barreirinhas or Atins. The lagoons fill with rain from roughly May and are

cities.name: Manaus
cities.base: Centro around the Largo de Sao Sebastiao and the Teatro Amazonas: the one part of the city that is pleasant on foot, five minutes from the market, and where the lodge vans collect you at 08:00. One ni

cities.name: Rio Negro jungle lodges (Novo Airao and the Anavilhanas)
cities.base: A lodge on the Rio Negro near Novo Airao, 3 hours by road from Manaus: black water means almost no mosquitoes and the Anavilhanas islands on the doorstep. Anavilhanas Jungle Lodge is the reference and

outings.name: Circuito Lagoa Azul
outings.why: 4x4 truck to the park gate, then a guided walk over the dunes to three to five lagoons and a swim; the afternoon slot (14:00 to 18:30) gets the low sun and fewer trucks, and in the dry months there is nothing to swim in.
outings.season: May to September for full lagoons; the drive runs all year
outings.fallback: The 4x4 still runs in rain; the sand track can flood in March and April and trucks turn back.

outings.name: Circuito Lagoa Bonita
outings.why: Same idea as Lagoa Azul but a steep 40-metre rope-assisted dune climb at the start and the classic sunset over the field of lagoons; 14:00 departure, back after dark.
outings.fallback: Skip it if you already did Lagoa Azul and the forecast is cloud; the point is the sunset.

outings.name: Rio Preguicas to Cabure (Vassouras, Mandacaru, Cabure)
outings.why: Speedboat down the river through mangrove to the Pequenos Lencois dunes at Vassouras, the Mandacaru lighthouse, and lunch on the Cabure sandbar between river and Atlantic; works in the dry season when the lagoons do not.
outings.fallback: None needed; the boat runs in rain and the stops are short.

outings.name: Canto do Atins (Lagoa Tropical, Lagoa da Esperanca, lunch at Seu Antonio)
outings.why: 4x4 along the beach from Atins to the eastern edge of the dune field, walk into the lagoons that hold water longest, and grilled shrimp at one of the two shacks at Canto do Atins; from Barreirinhas add the river boat both ways and it is the
outings.season: May to October (these lagoons outlast the Barreirinhas ones)
outings.fallback: Stay on the Atins beach and take the horse ride at 15:00 instead.

outings.name: Travessia dos Lencois (Atins to Santo Amaro via Queimada dos Britos and Baixa Gr
outings.why: A three-day walk across the dune field with a licensed guide, sleeping in hammocks at the two oasis settlements inside the park; 9 hours a day in loose sand with no shade, start at 05:00, and it only makes sense with full lagoons to swim in
outings.fallback: Do a one-day 4x4 out-and-back to Queimada dos Britos from Santo Amaro.

outings.name: Volta a Ilha boat (Garapua, Morere pools, Boipeba)

startsFrom.name: Morro de Sao Paulo, Terceira Praia

outings.why: Speedboat around Tinhare island: the Garapua reef pools, snorkelling at Morere on Boipeba at low tide, lunch on Boipeba, back through the Rio do Inferno mangrove; rough on the open-sea leg when the wind is up.
outings.season: All year, best on a low tide day between September and March
outings.fallback: The 4x4 to Garapua only, half a day.

outings.name: Quarta Praia low-tide walk to Praia do Encanto

startsFrom.name: Morro de Sao Paulo, Terceira Praia

outings.why: Walk the long beach south from Terceira Praia at low tide past the reef pools to the Praia do Encanto kiosks and back; check the tide table because the return along Quarta Praia disappears at high water.
outings.fallback: Stop at the Quarta Praia natural pools and turn round.

outings.name: Gamboa mud beach at low tide
outings.why: Walk from the village along the bay-side beach at low tide to the clay cliff at Gamboa where people paint themselves with the mud, then a boat back for a few reais; at high tide there is no beach and you go by boat both ways.

outings.name: Pelourinho Tuesday night (Olodum rehearsal)
outings.why: Terca da Bencao: the 18:00 blessing at Rosario dos Pretos, then Olodum drumming in the Praca das Artes and bands on every square until past midnight; the one night Pelourinho is full of locals, and the one night you can walk around it, thou
outings.season: All year, biggest from January to Carnival
outings.fallback: Balé Folclorico da Bahia at the Teatro Miguel Santana at 19:00 on Monday, Wednesday or Friday.

outings.name: Feira de Sao Joaquim and the Bonfim church
outings.why: Early taxi to the biggest open market in the city (candomble herbs, dende, live chickens, palm baskets), then up the peninsula to Bonfim for the ribbons on the railings and back along the Ribeira waterfront; go early, keep the phone in your
outings.season: All year; Friday is the Bonfim day and the market is fullest

outings.name: Encontro das Aguas from Porto da Ceasa
outings.why: Taxi 25 minutes east to the Ceasa port, hire a boatman from the cooperative there (R$20 a head with four people, R$80 for a smaller group), 10 minutes out to where the black Rio Negro runs beside the brown Solimoes without mixing; put a han
outings.season: All year; sharpest line in the dry months (September to Dece
outings.fallback: Most lodges pass it on the transfer boat, so if you are going to Juma you can skip this.

outings.name: MUSA tower in the Reserva Ducke
outings.why: 45-minute taxi north of the city, 242 steps up a steel tower to look over the canopy, then the orchid house and short trails; closed Wednesdays and the gate shuts at 16:00, go at 08:30 when the birds are up.
outings.fallback: Bosque da Ciencia at INPA in town, an hour with the otters and manatees.

outings.name: Anavilhanas archipelago by boat
outings.why: A full day in a covered boat through the 400-island river archipelago: swimming from a sandbank at low water, canoe into the flooded igapo at high water, herons and the occasional sloth; the lodge runs it as two half-day outings, ask for th
outings.season: All year; beaches September to January, flooded forest March
outings.fallback: Half-day canoe in the nearest igarape.

outings.name: Focagem: night caiman spotting by canoe
outings.why: Out at 20:00 with a guide and a torch, eyes glowing red along the bank, a small caiman lifted into the boat for a minute; the stars over black water are the real reason to go.
outings.fallback: None; it goes ahead unless there is lightning.

outings.name: Jungle trail with the lodge guide
outings.why: Three hours in terra firme forest behind the lodge: rubber tapping, ant nests, the medicinal trees, how to open a Brazil nut; you will not see big animals, and it is humid enough that the guide stops every ten minutes.

outings.name: Botos at the Novo Airao flutuante
outings.why: The pink river dolphins come to a floating platform on the Novo Airao waterfront to be fed on a schedule set by ICMBio; you stand in the water to your waist with them, no touching, a controlled and slightly zoo-like thing but the only near-
outings.fallback: Dolphins surface unprompted in the Anavilhanas channels most days.

places.name: Largo do Pelourinho and the Terreiro de Jesus
places.note: The painted colonial hill is the picture of Salvador and is worth two daylight hours, with the free Elevador Lacerda ride down to the lower city for the bay view at the end; it is heavily policed for a reason, so keep to the main squares, ignore the ribbon sellers, and leave before dark on any night

places.name: Igreja da Ordem Terceira de Sao Francisco
places.note: The carved sandstone facade and the blue tile cloister; the gilded Sao Francisco church next door, the famous one, is closed for restoration with no announced reopening date, so this is the one you can actually enter.

places.name: Museu Afro-Brasileiro (MAFRO)
places.note: The Carybe orixa panels alone are worth the R$10, and the candomble collection explains what you see in the market and on the street; weekdays only, small, an hour.

places.name: Terca da Bencao: Olodum in the Praca das Artes
places.note: Tuesday is the fixed night: blessing at Rosario dos Pretos at 18:00, Olodum's drum rehearsal in the square from around 19:00 (free or a small entry, it changes), and bands on every corner after; go with cash, no jewellery, and a taxi booked from the Praca da Se.

places.name: Balé Folclorico da Bahia, Teatro Miguel Santana
places.note: An hour of capoeira, orixa dances and fire in a small theatre, 19:00 on Monday, Wednesday and Friday in the 2026 season; it is for visitors, but it is well done, and it is the right way to see Pelourinho at night when it is not Tuesday.

places.name: Mercado Modelo
places.note: Two floors of the same fridge magnets and berimbaus at inflated prices, with hard-sell capoeira outside; the real market is Sao Joaquim, ten minutes up the coast.

places.name: Feira de Sao Joaquim
places.note: The city's working market: dende oil in reused bottles, candomble herbs and figures, dried shrimp for the acaraje, goats; go before 09:00, carry small notes, and it is fine with a bit of sense but not a place to wave a camera.

places.name: Acaraje da Dinha, Largo da Santana
places.note: The acaraje fried in dende on the square and split with vatapa, caruru, dried shrimp and as much pepper as you can take; Dinha's stall has a queue and Cira's across the square does not, and the difference between them is opinion.

places.name: Casa de Tereza
places.note: Tereza Paim's Bahian cooking done properly: moqueca de camarao, bobo, a crab moqueca on Fridays; open every day, book on WhatsApp for dinner, and the bill is about a third of what the same would cost in Rio.

places.name: Paraiso Tropical
places.note: A garden restaurant in an unglamorous suburb where the moqueca is made with fruit from the trees around you and the owner brings out things you have never tasted; lunch only, closed Monday, 25 minutes by taxi from Rio Vermelho and worth it.

places.name: JAM no MAM, Solar do Unhao
places.note: Saturday 18:00 jazz jam on the terrace of the modern art museum in a 17th-century sugar mill on the bay, R$8 in and the sun going down behind the stage; take a taxi both ways, the road outside is not one to walk after dark.

places.name: Porto da Barra beach and the Farol da Barra
places.note: The small city beach inside the bay where the whole neighbourhood swims after work and applauds the sunset, with the lighthouse fort a ten-minute walk along the seafront; rent a chair, buy a beer from the vendor, leave the phone at the hotel.

places.name: Segunda Praia
places.note: The busy beach: bar chairs to the water, football, caipirinhas at R$25, and the luau parties at night; fine for an afternoon and it is where the boats and the noise are, so sleep further along.

places.name: Quarta Praia and the natural pools
places.note: Two kilometres of coconut palms with almost nobody on it and reef pools you can snorkel in at low tide; the further you walk the emptier it gets, and the tide table decides whether the beach exists.

places.name: Praia do Encanto
places.note: The end of the walk south, mangrove behind, a couple of pousada kiosks for fried fish and beer, and the shallow warm water where the reef closes in; go by foot at low tide or by tractor-taxi from the village.

places.name: Fortaleza de Tapirandu (the Forte) at sunset
places.note: The 17th-century fort walls at the tip of the island, where the whole village goes at 17:30 to watch the sun drop into the bay and, from July to October, humpback whales spout offshore; it is a ruin, not a museum, go for the hour and then eat.

places.name: Tirolesa from the Farol to Primeira Praia
places.note: A 340-metre cable from the lighthouse hill straight into the sea off Primeira Praia, R$85 to R$95 a go and thirty seconds long; the climb up to the Mirante do Farol behind the church is worth doing anyway for the view down the beaches.

places.name: Gamboa mud cliff and beach
places.note: The fishing village on the calm bay side, reached on foot along the beach at low tide or by a five-minute boat, where you smear yourself with the grey clay from the cliff and rinse in water like a bath; it is a lark, and the beach bars are cheaper than Morro's.

places.name: Garapua and its reef pools
places.note: A fishing village on a bay south of the beaches with a wide natural pool in the reef at low tide; reached by 4x4 along the sand or as the first stop on the Volta a Ilha boat, and it is the quiet alternative to the boat day.

places.name: Boipeba and the Morere pools
places.note: The next island south, quieter than Morro by a decade, with snorkelling in the coral pools off Morere at low tide and lunch in the village; it is the whole day on the Volta a Ilha boat, and if you have three nights on the coast it is a better place to sleep than Morro.

places.name: Restaurante Sabor da Terra
places.note: The plain Bahian place on the main lane for a moqueca for two in a clay pot with rice, farofa and pirao; not refined, generous, and cheaper than anything on the beaches.

places.name: Minha Louca Paixao
places.note: The pousada restaurant on Terceira Praia that does seafood with some care, tables on the sand and a bill to match; it is where you eat on the last night, book ahead in high season.

places.name: Toca do Morcego
places.note: The clifftop bar below the lighthouse with the best sunset seat on the island and a DJ after dark; there is a cover charge that changes with the party, the drinks are dear, and the sunset from the fort next door is free.

places.name: Avenida Beira Rio at dusk
places.note: The riverside promenade along the Preguicas where the town walks, eats and watches the voadeiras come back after 18:00; it is the only thing to do in Barreirinhas itself and it is a pleasant enough hour.

places.name: Vassouras (Pequenos Lencois)
places.note: A stop on the river boat where the dunes come down to the water, a shack sells coconuts and tame monkeys are fed for tips; forty minutes is enough and it is the dunes without the lagoons.

places.name: Farol de Mandacaru
places.note: A navy lighthouse in a fishing village at the river mouth; climb the 160 steps for the view over the Preguicas delta, the Atlantic and the start of the dunes, buy a cashew sweet from the women at the bottom, and that is Mandacaru.

places.name: Cabure sandbar
places.note: A strip of sand between the calm river and the rough ocean with a handful of restaurants; lunch is grilled fish or shrimp at about R$100 for two, the river side is for swimming, the sea side is for walking, and the wind never stops.

places.name: Atins village
places.note: Sand streets, no bank, a dozen pousadas and a kitesurf crowd from July to December when the wind blows; the beach is a ten-minute walk and the dunes start behind the last houses, which is why people sleep here instead of Barreirinhas.

places.name: Praia de Atins and the river mouth
places.note: A wide flat beach where the Preguicas meets the sea, with kites in the air from midday in the windy months and nobody on it in the morning; the water is brown from the river and strong, swim in the lagoons instead.

places.name: Sunset horse ride from Atins
places.note: Three and a half hours on a local horse across the beach and up into the first dunes for the sunset, 15:00 out and back in the dark; the horses are small and the saddles basic, so it is for people who do not mind that.

places.name: A Canoa
places.note: The riverfront restaurant that claims to have invented shrimp served in a pineapple; the claim is doubtful, the shrimp are good, and it is the safe dinner in a town with few choices.

places.name: Bambae
places.note: Where locals send you for galinhada, the Maranhao chicken and rice, and grilled robalo; it will pick you up from your pousada for free, which tells you how far it is from the river.

places.name: Restaurante do Sr. Antonio, Canto do Atins
places.note: A palm-thatch shack at the edge of the dunes that grills whole shrimp over charcoal with urucum butter and serves them with rice on a plastic table; it is the meal of the Lencois, lunch only, and you only get here on the Canto do Atins 4x4.

places.name: Lagoa Azul
places.note: The lagoon everyone comes for, and it is as good as the photograph between June and September and a sand bowl in January; the 4x4 gate is 30 minutes from Barreirinhas, then an hour of walking on hot sand, so the 14:00 slot is the one to book.

places.name: Lagoa Bonita
places.note: The one with the rope up a 40-metre dune wall and the sunset from the top over the whole white field; fewer trucks than Lagoa Azul, longer walk, and it dries earlier in the year, ask what still has water before you book.

places.name: Lagoa da Esperanca
places.note: The big lagoon nearest Canto do Atins that keeps water into October when the Barreirinhas ones are gone; deep enough to swim properly, nobody selling anything, part of the Canto do Atins day.

places.name: Lagoa Tropical
places.note: A long green lagoon under a high dune ridge on the Atins side, reached on foot from the 4x4 drop; the guide takes you up the ridge first for the view and then you swim, which is the right order.

places.name: Queimada dos Britos oasis
places.note: A patch of cashew trees and a few families with hammocks for rent in the middle of the dune field, a day's walk from Atins or a hard 4x4 from Santo Amaro; sleeping here is the only way to have the lagoons to yourself at dawn, and there is no electricity.

places.name: Baixa Grande oasis
places.note: The second settlement on the crossing, a few houses around a permanent lake, one night in a hammock before the last walk out to Santo Amaro; only with a guide, only May to September, and only if 9 hours a day on sand sounds like a holiday.

places.name: Santo Amaro do Maranhao and Lagoa da Gaivota
places.note: The western entrance, a small town on a lake with dunes starting at the last street, where the lagoons hold water a month longer than at Barreirinhas; two and a half hours each way from Barreirinhas by 4x4, so most people who come here sleep here.

places.name: Lagoa das Emendadas
places.note: A chain of lagoons joined together on the Santo Amaro side, so you can swim from one to the next when they are full; the classic Santo Amaro afternoon, with the sunset from the dune above.

places.name: Dune sunset above the Atins sector
places.note: The last stop of any Atins-side outing: the driver parks under a dune at 17:15 and you walk up for the view over the lagoons with the sea behind; there is no shade all day, so this is when the sand is finally cool.

places.name: Teatro Amazonas
places.note: The 1896 rubber-boom opera house with the Italian marble and the dome of Alsatian tiles, a 30-minute guided visit for R$20, Tuesday to Sunday (Sunday closes at 13:00), closed Monday; if the Amazonas Philharmonic is playing that night the tickets are cheap and you should go.

places.name: Tacaca da Gisela, Largo de Sao Sebastiao
places.note: Tacaca from a gourd on the square at dusk: hot tucupi broth, jambu leaves that numb your mouth, dried shrimp and tapioca gum; it is the Manaus thing to eat and the best introduction to what the region tastes like.

places.name: Mercado Municipal Adolpho Lisboa
places.note: The 1883 iron market copied from Les Halles, restored, with the fish hall (tambaqui, pirarucu, jaraqui) at its best before 09:00 and stalls of tucuma, cupuacu and guarana sticks; open daily, Sundays only until noon.

places.name: Feira da Manaus Moderna and the floating port
places.note: The working fish and produce market behind the Adolpho Lisboa where the river boats unload at dawn, with the hammock boats to Belem and Tabatinga tied up alongside; loud, wet underfoot, over by 10:00, and the real port of Manaus.

places.name: Encontro das Aguas
places.note: The black Negro and the sandy Solimoes run side by side for kilometres without mixing, and from a small boat out of the Ceasa port you can put a hand in each; the agency version adds a floating restaurant and a caged sloth and is worth avoiding, the R$20 boatman version is not.

places.name: MUSA, Museu da Amazonia (canopy tower)
places.note: A 42-metre tower above the canopy in a real forest reserve on the city's edge, plus an orchid house and a serpentarium, R$40 without a guide; closed Wednesday, last entry 16:00, and a 45-minute taxi each way.

places.name: Bosque da Ciencia (INPA)
places.note: The research institute's forest park in town with manatees, giant otters and free-roaming agoutis, an hour's walk in shade; closed Monday, and weekday hours have a lunch break, so mornings are safest.

places.name: Museu do Seringal Vila Paraiso
places.neighborhood: Igarape Sao Joao, across the Rio Negro
places.note: A reconstructed rubber baron's estate on a creek across the river, built as a film set and kept as a museum, showing how the tappers were kept in debt; 20 minutes by boat from the Marina do Davi at Ponta Negra, a small entry fee, closed Monday, and the only place that explains why the opera house ex

places.name: Banzeiro
places.note: Felipe Schaedler's restaurant that put Amazonian cooking on the map: tambaqui ribs, pirarucu with tucupi, a tucuma ice cream; open every day with a break between 15:30 and 18:30, book, and it is the one expensive meal in the north that earns it.

places.name: Caxiri
places.note: Regional cooking in a restored house on the opera-house square, pirarucu and tambaqui done in a few ways and Amazonian fruit in everything; walkable from a Centro hotel, which after dark matters in Manaus.

places.name: Ponta Negra beach and promenade
places.note: The city's river beach on the Negro, a real sand beach from September to January and a promenade of bars the rest of the year, 30 minutes from the centre; go for a sunset beer and the black water, not for a swim on a busy Sunday.

places.name: Palacio Rio Negro
places.note: A German rubber trader's mansion that became the governor's palace, now a free cultural centre with period rooms and rotating shows; a cool 45 minutes on the walk between the market and the theatre, closed Monday.

places.name: Anavilhanas archipelago by boat
places.note: Four hundred islands of flooded forest in the Rio Negro, the second largest river archipelago on earth; from a lodge at Novo Airao the boat is in it within twenty minutes, and the day is included in the price.

places.name: Igapo canoe in the flooded forest
places.note: Paddling between the tree trunks with the water ten metres up them, silent, monkeys and hoatzins above; this is the Amazon people imagine and it only exists from about March to August, in the dry months the same forest is a walk.

places.name: Piranha fishing
places.note: A bamboo pole, a bit of beef, and a guide who catches five to your none; the lodge kitchen will fry what you land, and it is a lodge staple rather than anything wild, but the afternoon on the water is the point.

places.name: Focagem de jacare (night caiman spotting)
places.note: Out after dinner with a torch to find the red eyes along the bank; the guide usually lifts a small spectacled caiman into the canoe, which you can decline, and the stars over the black river with the engine off are the better half of the outing.

places.name: Terra firme jungle trail
places.note: A guided three hours on a forest trail learning what the trees and ants are for, in long trousers and closed shoes; expect insects and sweat rather than jaguars, and go in the morning before the heat.

places.name: Flutuante dos Botos, Novo Airao
places.note: The pink dolphins arrive at the floating deck at feeding times fixed by ICMBio and you stand in the water with them for fifteen minutes; it is regulated feeding of wild animals, which you may or may not be comfortable with, and it is the one close encounter you can count on.

places.name: Sunrise canoe on the Rio Negro
places.neighborhood: Rio Negro, in front of the lodge
places.note: Wake at 05:00 for a slow paddle when the mist is on the water and the birds are loudest: toucans, macaws going over in pairs, kingfishers; the best two hours of any lodge stay and the one most people sleep through.

places.name: Ribeirinho community visit (lodge-arranged)
places.note: A boat to a riverside family's house to see manioc being grated, pressed and toasted into farinha, with crafts for sale at the end; every lodge runs a version and the value depends entirely on your guide and how many others are in the boat.

places.name: Rio Negro sandbank swim at low water
places.note: From September to January the river drops fifteen metres and leaves white sand beaches in the archipelago where you swim in warm tea-coloured water with no piranhas that will bother you and no mosquitoes; in the high-water months these beaches do not exist.

places.name: Lodge dinner: tambaqui, pirarucu and the fruit table
places.note: Meals are included and at the better lodges are the Amazonian menu done well: grilled tambaqui ribs, pirarucu in tucupi, farinha, and a breakfast table of cupuacu, tucuma and pupunha you will not see again; drinks are extra and priced like an airport.

places.name: Novo Airao waterfront and boatyards
places.note: The small river town where the wooden Amazon boats are still built on the beach and the sun sets straight down the Negro; an hour's walk if the lodge takes you in for the dolphins, and a look at where the guides actually live.
